desc: The root table: the action space available_actions(member, role, state) enumerates. Each action kind carries the roles that can take it and an admissibility expression; the function returns, for every member, every action whose expression is true, with justification = the satisfied conjuncts (each carrying its citation). Recomputed on every event. Bindings: member = the acting member; m/t/q as noted per action.

function.justification: by construction: the admissibility expression's satisfied conjuncts with their cite annotations; for blocked actions (when asked why-not), the true out-of-order disjunct with its cite

params: time (target time carried by the motion's content — postpone/fix-time/recess/schedule forms; null otherwise)
series (the consecutive-series scope named by the mover — limit-extend-debate, previous-question, division-of-question qualified forms; null = immediately pending only)
actions.desc: make a motion; instantiated once per motion id currently admissible
actions.quorum_note: the third quorum disjunct carries 40:7's remainder: measures to obtain a quorum, plus subsidiary/incidental motions, questions of privilege, and the orders call when related to the allowed motions or to the conduct of the inquorate meeting — a judgment-shaped relatedness test, routed
actions.note: demanding-class motions (division-of-assembly, call-for-orders-of-the-day) and requests are included: their registry second=false plus interrupt attributes make them available without the floor

actions.desc: rise and address the chair to seek recognition
actions.note: who WINS recognition is protocol.json preference_in_recognition, applied by the chair among timely claims (guard/preference-claim-timely)

counter limits modifiable by special rules or orders (protocol.json speech_counters); appeal's compiled exception — one speech per member, chair twice [24:3(5)] — also governs points of order submitted to the assembly (the frame's motion id remains point-of-order; its debate follows appeal rules [23:19]): stage-5 sets the appeal branch for submitted points too

the chair (if a member) votes when by ballot, or exactly when the vote would affect the result — compiled for majority (break or cause a tie) and two-thirds (cause or block attainment: yes+1 = 2·no, or yes = 2·no); other thresholds analogous by their threshold_evaluation expressions; never twice [44:12]. The tally here is the standing count at the chair's decision point (voice/rising votes: after the negative). Already-voted exclusion and method mechanics (roll-call order, ballot distribution) remain stage-5 orchestration over the Vote record

no second and no recognition required unless also speaking in debate [46:6]; on objection, no one nominates a second person until every member wishing to nominate has had opportunity, and never more persons than places to fill [46:6]. election_pending marks a pending election question; nominations-closed is set by motion/motions-relating-to-nominations

single-member demand splitting an independent-subject series or a non-conforming amendment series — no motion, no vote; interrupt-capable [42:18(d)]. The two series flags are recorded question structure (from the motion's text at making)
the chair's duty on noticing the absence; thereafter only the 40:7 action set is admissible (move's quorum disjuncts)

no vote changes under ballot or any other secrecy-providing method [45:8] — ballot is the only secret method in the current enum; extend the exclusion list with any added secret method. After announcement a change is reachable only via the request action (unanimous consent, requested immediately while guard/result-window-open) — deliberately not a disjunct here.
window opens when the negative votes have been cast, not at the first affirmative vote [29:4(1)]
timely even immediately after the chair's announcement of the consent action
before stating: unilateral; after: becomes a consent/vote exchange (protocol.json requests)
any member may call up (no second) [37:9(4)]; if the target would be in order mid-series it slots per precedence.json reconsider_split_rank
the adjudication entry point (adjudication.json machine, raise)
needs a second (two members together); debatability and yields per adjudication.json and table/appeal-yield-matrix

params: q (the ignored point of order, appeal, or motion)
actions.desc: the chair-stonewall remedy: after the chair has repeatedly ignored a duly made point of order, appeal, or motion, the member — standing in place — puts the question to a vote without debate, without the chair
actions.note: counts per 62:8-9: a point of order is repeated a second and third time (three ignorings) then put ('Is the point of order that… well taken?'); an appeal is repeated to a third making, each seconded, then put ('Shall the decision of the chair be sustained?'); the ignored-motion variant of 62:8 — repeat the original motion, seconded, still ignored — needs two ignorings. Undebatable; thresholds per the ignored question's own rules. Rights-critical: the assembly's last-resort enforcement against a chair who will not act — every other remedy in the model routes through the chair. Pinned for phase-7 (never rank-buried). Escalation beyond it: temporary removal of the chair [62:10], declare-the-chair-vacant against a chair pro tem [62:11]

a brief pause without declaring recess — technically no interruption of the meeting; used e.g. to consult before ruling on a point of order [23:3] or with the parliamentarian [47:51]; ends on the chair's word or any member's objection
single-member affordance; the objection ends the pause immediately (event/stand-at-ease-ended)
the chair's alternative — rule out of order — is the same decision point's other branch

debate exhaustion is derived, not an event: undebatable question, an order closing debate, or no timely floor claim for debate (members whose counters are exhausted cannot make a timely claim — speak-in-debate governs claims)
which claimant is ENTITLED is protocol.json preference_in_recognition; recognizing another is a breach remediable by point of order [42:15]
preemption of a pending question additionally requires guard/may-preempt (scheduler.json)

params: item (the report's slot in the order of business / reports queue)
actions.note: motions on behalf of the committee need no second [4:11]

chair_duty_note: Chair actions are duties as much as options: where exactly one chair action is admissible (announce the known next item [41:24], state a seconded in-order motion promptly [4:16]), the list is also the obligation. The model exposes admissibility; duty sequencing is stage-5 policy over the same expressions.
